messages:
Morgan: Quick design check — I'm leaning toward a connector-lite model for private endpoints: minimal control plane surface (only auth/token exchange + metrics) in our control plane, and a thin tenant-side connector that handles NAT/DNS and mTLS termination. Tradeoffs: simpler CP, lower cross-account peering complexity, but shifts routing/egress logic to tenant side. Thoughts?

Raj: I like the smaller CP footprint, but major concern is cert distribution and rotation to the tenant connector. How do we avoid a central cert-sync that recreates a peering-like trust surface?

Tess: We can use short-lived tokens + on-demand client cert issuance from CP KMS. Connector fetches cert over HTTPS with mutual TLS using a bootstrap token. No static long-lived peering creds.

Morgan: @Tess that's what I was imagining. Also want to avoid hairpin NAT in customer VPCs — connector should SNAT to a per-tenant egress IP when required. That means connector needs control plane signals for egress allocation but not full config replication.

Raj: Per-tenant egress IP management is fine, but emitting those IP allocations from CP implies a stateful mapping service. We should consider an allocation API (CRUD) rather than pushing full routing tables.

Yuval: Allocation API + lease model seems right. Connector requests a lease for an egress IP range; CP returns allocation + TTL. Connector renews before TTL. If CP can't allocate, connector falls back to managed relay in our region. That gives graceful degradation.

Morgan: Agree on fallback. Also need a small health/trace surface so ops can see per-tenant latency and errors without exposing tenant traffic. Proposal: metrics shippers from connector to CP metrics pipeline via pre-signed, short-lived ingest URLs.

Tess: That avoids peering for observability. But we need to think about debugging—packet-level traces won't be available unless tenant opts into more invasive telemetry (e.g., packet capture agent). Document that as opt-in.

Raj: Security note — any TLS termination in tenant VPC must preserve customer key custody expectations. We can't request plaintext or private keys. Connector must perform termination locally with keys never leaving tenant. CP cert issuance only provides cert; private key generation lives in connector.

Morgan: Good call. So flow: 1) Connector bootstrap with bootstrap token; 2) local keypair generation; 3) CSR -> CP CA via mutual-auth; 4) CP returns cert signed short-lived; 5) connector uses cert for mTLS to our gateways or for local termination.

Yuval: For connectivity patterns where customers prefer no outbound to public internet, we should support a relay appliance (managed by us) inside customer VPC (subscription) or use VPC endpoints to CP. But both add ops burden. Mark as advanced mode.

Tess: Rollout plan suggestion: start with small alpha customers using connector-lite + allocation API + managed fallback relay. Measure control plane load, allocation churn, and latency. If allocation churn high, consider batching leases per AZ.

Morgan: Ok next steps: write a short RFC with sequence diagrams (bootstrap, lease, renew, fallback), a minimal API sketch for /v1/leases, and a security checklist for key custody. I'll draft and ping here.

infra-bot: New doc created: docs/proposals/connector-lite-lease-model.md (link) :white_check_mark:

Raj: Thanks — please include a section on SLOs for fallback activation window and owner oncall runbook for lease exhaustion.

Morgan: Will do. Thanks all.
